bullets.text: The US has imposed new sanctions on Iran and its trading partners, leading to strong criticism from China, which is a major buyer of Iranian oil. This move further escalates tensions and threatens to isolate nations continuing business with Tehran.

A global crackdown on West African cyber-crime networks has led to mass arrests, including 39 individuals in South Africa for romance and investment scams. This operation targets widespread online fraudulent activities originating from the region.

In Nigeria, the president has ordered a manhunt after kidnappers uploaded a video showing dozens of men, women, and children held captive in a forest. This follows an attack on worshippers in Dekara village where hundreds were reportedly taken.
The Plymouth Brethren Christian Church is seeking to establish its fifth church in Kyneton, Victoria, for 45 members, 87 kilometres north-west of Melbourne.
Two Victorian police officers who were shot dead a year ago in Porepunkah are being honoured with memorial gardens and commemorations.
Australia may experience a surge in data centre construction as AI firms aim to circumvent upcoming regulations requiring new sites to incorporate renewable energy and minimise water usage.
Canada has announced $20 billion in retaliatory tariffs on hundreds of US goods, escalating a trade dispute with the US, which will take effect on September 8.
Foot Locker's owner experienced a significant drop in shares after warning that nervous consumers are cutting back on spending due to the current geopolitical environment.
Oil prices declined amid renewed diplomatic efforts to prevent an escalation of the Iran conflict and discussions regarding the Strait of Hormuz, easing inflation concerns.
